title: Half the Roof, Whole the Bill
covers: how to find the area of a triangle as half of a rectangle or parallelogram with the same base and perpendicular height
cert: finding the area of triangles using A = ½ × base × height and spotting missing-half errors

intro.caption: Lesson 5-2 — area of triangles. Someone billed the guildhall double for painting its triangular sign. Three reader gates and a counter showdown stand between the crew and a fair bill.

balloons.t: Whoa! Our triangle sign was billed for double the paint we actually used!
Blurb! Expensive paper. Needs more salt.
Put two matching triangles together and you get a rectangle: base times height.
So ONE triangle is always half of that rectangle!

pages.caption: A triangle is half of a rectangle or parallelogram with the same base and height: A = ½ × b × h.

balloons.t: Check the gable triangle first: base 12, perpendicular height 7. Remember the half!
Watch out for slanted edges! Only the 90-degree height counts in ½ × b × h.
Blurb! Right-triangle legs already meet at 90 degrees!
Okay, I wrote 160 for a 20-by-8 triangle sign! What did I miss?
You paid for the whole rectangle, Dree. A triangle is half!
Base 18, height 10, at 4 gold per square block. Pay up 720 gold!
Hold it. That's a triangle sign, not a rectangle!
360 gold saved, half the paint, and twice as shiny!

win.caption: Every triangle is half of a rectangle or parallelogram with the same base and perpendicular height, so A = ½ × b × h.

gates.title: Gate 1 · Compose a Parallelogram
gates.prompt: Use the two-triangles trick to find the area of one triangle.
hints: Conceptual: two identical triangles make one parallelogram (or rectangle) with area b × h, so one triangle is half of that.
Procedural: multiply base × perpendicular height, then divide by 2.

steps: One triangle is half: 40 ÷ 2 = 20 square blocks.
worked.q: A triangle has base 10 and height 6. What is its area?

items.q: Two identical triangles fit together to make a parallelogram with area 48 square blocks. What is the area of ONE triangle?

options.fb: 48 is the area of BOTH triangles together. Divide by 2 for one triangle.
96 doubles the parallelogram instead of taking half.
12 is one-fourth of 48. Two triangles make one parallelogram, so take one-half.

items.label: Gable triangle area (base = 12, height = 7):
items.aria: area of gable triangle in square blocks

fb.msg: 84 is 12 × 7, the whole rectangle! A triangle is half of that rectangle.
19 is 12 + 7. Multiply base by height, then take half.

gates.pass: Forty-two square blocks! Half the rectangle, half the paint.

gates.title: Gate 2 · Compute with Height
gates.prompt: Find the area of the banner and the right-triangle brace. Watch out for slanted edges!
hints: Conceptual: only the perpendicular (90°) height counts; in a right triangle, the two legs are already perpendicular.
Procedural: multiply ½ × base × perpendicular height.

steps: Practice triangle: base = 9, slanted edge = 7, perpendicular height = 4.
Skip the slanted 7; use base 9 and height 4.
worked.q: A triangle has base 7 and perpendicular height 8. Find its area.

items.label: Banner (base = 14, slant = 11, height = 6). Area =
items.aria: area of triangular banner in square blocks

fb.msg: 84 is 14 × 6 without the ½. Take half for a triangle.
77 is ½ × 14 × 11, using the slanted side. Use the perpendicular height (6).
154 used the slanted side AND forgot the ½.

items.label: Right-triangle brace (legs 9 and 8). Area =
items.aria: area of right triangle brace in square blocks

fb.msg: 72 is 9 × 8, the whole rectangle. Remember to multiply by ½.
17 is 9 + 8. Use A = ½ × b × h.

gates.pass: 42 and 36 square blocks. Kai rolls up his tape measure.

gates.title: Gate 3 · Find the Culprit
gates.badge: Bill Detective — Spot the Missing Half
gates.prompt: Dree billed 160 square blocks for a triangle sign with base 20 and height 8. Diagnose the mistake and fix it.
hints: Conceptual: forgetting ½ doubles the triangle's area into a full rectangle.
Procedural: check 20 × 8 = 160, then take half of 160.

steps: True triangle area = ½ × 66 = 33 square blocks.
worked.q: Someone billed 66 for a base-11, height-6 triangle. What is the true area?

items.q: What went wrong with Dree's 160 square-block estimate for a 20-by-8 triangle?

options.t: She multiplied 20 × 8 and forgot to multiply by ½
She used the perimeter instead of the area
options.fb: 20 × 8 is a multiplication of base and height, not adding sides.
Dividing by 2 twice would make the answer smaller (40), not 160.

items.label: True area of the 20-by-8 triangle sign:
items.aria: true area of the 20 by 8 triangle sign

fb.msg: 160 is Dree's whole-rectangle number. Take half!

gates.pass: 80 square blocks! Case solved — Dree admits she forgot the ½.

gates.title: Boss Gate · Settle the Bill
gates.prompt: The Champs billed 720 gold for painting the main triangle sign (base 18, height 10) at 4 gold per square block. Settle the real bill!
hints: Conceptual: find the triangle's true area first using ½ × b × h, then multiply by the cost per square block.
Procedural: Area = ½ × 18 × 10. Then multiply that area by 4 gold.

steps: Practice sign: base = 6, height = 10, cost = 2 gold per square block.
worked.q: A triangle sign has base 8, height 5, and costs 3 gold per square block. Total cost?

items.label: Lock 1 · True area (base = 18, height = 10):
items.aria: true area of main triangle sign

fb.msg: 180 is 18 × 10, the full rectangle. A triangle is half of that.

items.label: Lock 2 · True paint bill (90 sq blocks × 4 gold):

fb.msg: 720 is 180 × 4 — that's The Champs' doubled bill!
94 is 90 + 4. Multiply the area by 4 gold per square block.

items.fbDefault: Multiply 90 square blocks by 4 gold each.

items.q: Lock 3 · Why was The Champs' 720-gold invoice double the real price?

options.t: They charged 8 gold per square block instead of 4
options.fb: They used 4 gold per block, but on 180 square blocks instead of 90.

options.t: They billed for the full 18 × 10 rectangle instead of half for a triangle
They measured the slanted side twice
options.fb: They used base 18 and height 10, just without the ½.

gates.pass: 90 square blocks, 360 gold! The clerk stamps PAID IN FULL, and The Champs walk out empty-handed.

journal.heading: Lesson 5-2 — what the triangle bill taught us
rows: Two identical triangles make a rectangle or parallelogram, so one triangle is ½ × base × height.
A = ½ × b × h (or (b × h) ÷ 2). Both give the exact same area.
Measure height straight at 90° to the base — never use a slanted side.
Forgetting the ½ doubles the area and doubles the bill!
journal.quote: "Half the rectangle, half the paint, and half the paper for me to snack on." — Gel

teacher.suggested: Use during or after lesson 5-2 (Determine the Area of Triangles). Whole-class on a projector, pairs on devices, or independent practice. Covers deriving A = ½ × b × h from rectangles/parallelograms, identifying perpendicular height, and diagnosing missing-half errors.
standards: Derive a formula for the area of a right triangle using a rectangle; find the area of triangles and special quadrilaterals by decomposing or composing
